A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OVSegDT and contain the same complete 14-page paper, including the reproducibility checklist and six appendix sections. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original HM3D-OVON navigation experiments, component ablations, training analyses, and statistical comparisons in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains these original empirical results, including the OVSegDT benchmark results in Table 1 and observation-component experiments in appendix Table 11.

M1.justification: Both versions specify the same transformer architecture, binary goal-mask encoder, auxiliary segmentation objective, EALM loss modulation, and adaptation to YOLOE segmentation. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HM3D-OVON training and evaluation coverage, including seen, seen-synonym, and unseen categories. Ground-truth-mask, predicted-mask, and observation-component test scenarios are retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same ten comparison methods, including Uni-NaVid, VLFM, DAgRL+OD, TANGO, and MTU3D. Table 2 also retains the same PPO, DAgger, DAgger+PPO, EarlySwitcher, and DAgRL comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation splits, SR/SPL/collision metrics, training budgets, model configurations, and testing procedures are unchanged. Both versions retain the 200M-step training setup with 40 environments and the same appendix configurations.

E4.justification: The same training-strategy, goal-mask, segmentation-loss, and predicted-segmentation ablations appear in Tables 2-4. The appendix retains the same confidence-threshold analyses, training curves, and mask-versus-text input ablation in Table 11.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed means and standard deviations. Appendix Section 5 retains three runs per algorithm and the same one-sided t-test for unpaired samples, with unchanged statistical reporting in Tables 8-10.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and plotted findings match. For example, Table 1 retains OVSegDT's val-unseen SR of 40.1 ± 1.1 and SPL of 20.9 ± 0.9; appendix Table 11 retains SR values of 70.4, 65.3, and 0.1 for full, mask-only, and text-only observations.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation and Equations 1-9, including the entropy gate and combined training objective, are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about segmentation-guided navigation, EALM, generalization, sample efficiency, and collision reduction. No claim is added, strengthened, or narrowed.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of segmentation cues, training behavior, and ablation tradeoffs. The limitations concerning segmentation quality and inability to follow free-form text instructions are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, mask-filtering thresholds, hyperparameters in Tables 5-7, hardware/software specifications, and the code-access statement are identical. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list contain the same works and research positioning. The distinctions from map-based methods, other mapless policies, and prior auxiliary-task approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page affiliations change from AIRI and Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology, with postal addresses, to Cognitive AI Systems Lab and MIRAI. The arXiv version/date stamp also updates; body wording and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-10 and Tables 1-11 retain their content, captions, formatting, and placement. The main-text and appendix layouts are preserved; extraction-spacing differences do not indicate redesigned displays.

improvement.justification: v2.pdf updates affiliations and the version/date stamp while preserving the scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and visual organization, including the appendices. These administrative edits establish no meaningful overall quality improvement or deterioration.
